facts.text: Kapolei is nicknamed Oahu’s Second City, a title it earned in 1977 when the state officially recognized it as the island’s second urban center.
Kapolei’s land was once part of the estate of industrialist James Campbell, whose legacy lives on in the area’s development plans.
The region that is now Kapolei was built on former sugarcane and pineapple fields, reflecting Hawaii’s agricultural past.
Kapolei Property Development, a subsidiary of the James Campbell Company, has been the primary developer shaping the community’s modern skyline.
The original master plan called for a smart city with energy‑efficient technologies, walkable streets, and a hub for government and business offices.
